- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > 0.0), model frequently overestimates downward trend → adjust downward bias by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion when sentiment is volatile → apply 1–3% upward bias to forecast mean over 10-day horizon.
- When sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to lag → add 1–2% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70.00, model often overpredicts → apply 3–5% downward correction if sentiment is flat or mildly negative.
